$comment: Phase 2 dry-run config. dry_run is hard-coded true — see docs/04-architecture/execution-freqtrade.md. Never flip this to false by hand; a promotion to live is a Conductor-issued config change (Phase 3+), not a manual edit.

order_types.$comment: Limit entry/exit prefers maker fills per docs/04-architecture/execution-freqtrade.md ('Order preference'); stoploss stays market so it always fills.

telegram.$comment: Status-only mode (work package 2D, hardened in a follow-up review). Token/chat_id are blank here and injected via FREQTRADE__TELEGRAM__TOKEN / FREQTRADE__TELEGRAM__CHAT_ID env vars (same blank-in-config pattern as api_server below) -- see infra/README.md 'Telegram bot (status-only)'. Deliberately a SEPARATE bot/token from the Conductor bot reserved in .env.example's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (Phase 3+). IMPORTANT, read infra/README.md before trusting this label: Freqtrade 2026.8 has NO config-level per-command permission system -- verified directly against freqtrade/rpc/telegram.py and rpc.py (work package 2D follow-up). Every command it registers (including /forceexit, /stop, /stopbuy, /delete, /reload_config, /pause, /blacklist_delete) is reachable by anyone who can message this bot as the configured chat_id -- `keyboard` below only restricts which buttons the Telegram client SHOWS, it does not block a manually-typed command. The one command that IS genuinely blocked server-side, regardless of the keyboard, is /forcebuy and /forceshort, via force_entry_enable: false below (confirmed live against the running instance, verified in freqtrade/rpc/rpc.py `_rpc_force_entry`). `allow_custom_messages: false` disables the strategy's own ability to push arbitrary custom messages, unrelated to incoming commands. Real enforcement of 'status-only' rests on keeping the token/chat_id private (risk register S4) and on every other reachable command being risk-neutral-or-reducing (stop/pause/delete/reload never increase exposure) -- not on a technical command block Freqtrade doesn't provide.

api_server.$comment: Bound to 0.0.0.0 inside the container; infra/docker-compose.yml publishes it to the host as 127.0.0.1:8080 only. Credentials are blank here and injected at runtime via FREQTRADE__API_SERVER__* env vars (see .env.example) so no secret is committed.
